comment: The judged half of tools/matcheck.py. A ruling says which material a surface ought to
wear, where no checker could work that out: the glTF material name is MU's texture sheet
rather than a library entry, or it names a library entry that is simply the wrong choice.
A ruling either names a library material from index.json, which keeps it traced, or gives
roughness and metal outright -- which is an invention, and PLAN.md's rule is that an
invention says why. Once a ruling exists the audit is mechanical again: the slot's baked
ORM must match its ruling, and drift fails the run.
A ruling is a statement of what ought to be, not a change to what is. Nothing in the
engine reads this file yet -- see docs/materials.md, 'Applying a ruling'. Until that is
built, a ruling here makes matcheck fail on the slot until the content is repaired, which
is the honest state: the wrong material is still on screen.
